subject: Shortfall contingency, rate-swap option, and credit timeline
messages:
From: Sophie Carter <sophie@brightcart.com>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: BrightCart Billing <billing@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Shortfall contingency — unexpected spike this morning

Hi Hiro,

We had an unexpected traffic spike during our morning batch jobs that consumed about 3.4x our normal token volume for the hour. Our platform team attached the usage extract for Q2 so you can see the delta.

We need help on two things:
- Temporary headroom for the remainder of this billing window (we're expecting elevated traffic through Saturday due to a partner promotion).
- A clean path for the overrun: whether Redwood can offer a rate-swap (convert the overage into discounted committed capacity for the next quarter) or a one-time credit to soften the invoice impact.

Ideally we'd like something that:
1) gives immediate throughput allowance so we don't hit throttles;
2) keeps the billing impact from spiking our month close; and
3) has a clear timeline and PO path so our finance team can accept it.

Attached: BrightCart_Q2_usage_report.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Appreciate a quick flag on whether this is workable.

Thanks,
Sophie Carter
Head of Platform
BrightCart

From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
To: Sophie Carter <sophie@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shortfall contingency — unexpected spike this morning

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and for the usage extract. I reviewed the CSV and see the short window spike you described. Short answer: yes, we can help.

Two pragmatic options we can move on immediately:

Option A — Temporary headroom + pro-rata billing
- We lift your quota by a short-term buffer today (effective immediately) so you won't hit hard throttles.
- Usage will be invoiced at standard overrun rates; we can apply a one-time usage credit to offset part of the spike once we reconcile final numbers next week.

Option B — Rate-swap amendment (recommended for minimal invoice volatility)
- Convert the measured overrun into a discounted committed increase for the next 3 months.
- We apply an up-front credit equal to 30% of the calculated overrun and reduce per-token pricing on the swapped volume for the commit period.
- This preserves your runway, keeps month-end invoices predictable, and gives Redwood committed traction for capacity planning.

Logistics/proposed timeline:
- Today: we can enable a temporary +40% headroom to avoid throttles.
- Wed (6/13): final reconciliation of the spike and draft of the amendment term sheet (I attached a short form).
- Thu (6/14): Ben can send the DocuSign for the amendment; PO can be attached to the DocuSign packet.
- Next invoice: credit applied to offset part of the overrun per the term sheet.

I've attached a short term sheet for Option B: proposed-rate-swap-term-sheet.pdf (summary of pricing and credit mechanics). Ben — can you confirm the billing mechanics and whether we should route the initial escrow invoice to BrightCart Billing?

Sophie — if Option B looks acceptable, confirm and we will start the paperwork today. If you prefer the simpler credit + headroom path, say so and we'll fast-track it.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed-rate-swap-term-sheet.pdf (pdf, 48KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Carter <sophie@brightcart.com>, hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shortfall contingency — unexpected spike this morning

Hi Sophie / Hiro — looping in the billing mechanics here so there's no surprise at month close.

Quick notes on implementation (Option B flow, rate-swap):
- We will generate an escrow-style invoice covering the expected swapped volume. That invoice can be paid or PO'd by BrightCart; once the amendment is signed the escrow will be applied to future invoices.
- The 30% one-time credit Hiro mentioned will be applied as a line-item credit on the next invoice after reconciliation.
- If the swapped volume is lower than the actual overrun during reconciliation, we will invoice the delta at the agreed overrun rate and then apply the credit proportionally.

DocuSign and timing:
- I will prepare the DocuSign amendment and include a field for your PO number. The link will have the amendment and the billing addendum. Expect the DocuSign link Thursday morning.

Billing contacts: please make sure BrightCart Billing (billing@brightcart.com) is authorized to accept invoices and PO documents. If you'd prefer the credit applied immediately to the open invoice instead of escrow, we can do that — it just requires sign-off from your finance team.

On quoting the prior thread for context:
> On Tue, Jun 12, 2028 at 10:05 AM hiro_tanaka@redwood.com wrote:
> > Two pragmatic options we can move on immediately:
> > Option A — Temporary headroom + pro-rata billing
> > Option B — Rate-swap amendment (recommended for minimal invoice volatility)

Let me know which path BrightCart prefers and I'll issue the DocuSign and provisional invoice.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Carter <sophie@brightcart.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, BrightCart Billing <billing@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shortfall contingency — unexpected spike this morning

Hiro / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. We discussed this with finance and procurement.

BrightCart accepts Option B (rate-swap amendment) with the 30% credit and the 3-month committed uplift. Two quick asks before DocuSign:
1) Can you cap the swapped volume at the reconciled overrun figure (we don't want a permanent uplift in case traffic normalizes)?
2) Please include a clause that any unused swapped volume after the 3-month window converts back to standard pay-as-you-go at the original rates (no automatic carryover).

Attached: BrightCart_PO_5567.pdf (PO number 5567) — procurement will route payment once the DocuSign package has the PO attached.

If you can send the DocuSign with those two clauses included, procurement will sign and we can move forward.

Thanks again — appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Sophie Carter
Head of Platform
BrightCart

[Attachment: BrightCart_PO_5567.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]
